messages:
ACME Oncall: Hey team — after last night's scheduled cert rotation for private.redwood.acme.svc our internal services started seeing intermittent 401s and occasional 504s. Rolling back the endpoint to the old cert/VIP made things normal again. Can you help triage?

Kevin (Support): Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste one failing request log or a quick curl -v from the failing host? Also did you get any rotator events?

ACME Oncall: Pasting minimal curl output from an app host inside our VPC that hits the Private endpoint:

```
$ curl -v https://private.redwood.acme.svc/health -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" --resolve private.redwood.acme.svc:443:10.20.1.5
* Connected to private.redwood.acme.svc (10.20.1.5) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* ERROR: SSL: certificate verify failed (unable to get local issuer certificate)
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL: certificate verify failed (unable to get local issuer certificate)
```

We also see occasional 401s in our app logs: `http: auth failed: token ok but tls verify failed`

rotator-bot: rotation completed for tenant=acme uploaded_bundle=cb-2026-03-16-08:23 status=success

Oliver K.: Thanks — two quick checks: 1) what does openssl s_client show from inside the VPC (the failing one) vs from a public host? 2) can you confirm if you have a TLS inspection / proxy that terminates or rewrites TLS?

ACME Oncall: We do have a corporate TLS-inspector appliance (inline) on egress that performs SNI rewrite and payload inspection. I ran openssl from an internal host and from our bastion (outside the inspector). Outputs below — internal shows only the leaf, external shows full chain.

Internal (failing host behind inspector):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.acme.svc:443 -servername private.redwood.acme.svc -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = private.redwood.acme.svc
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:CN = private.redwood.acme.svc
   i:CN = Redwood Intermediate CA (TRUNCATED)
---
No client certificate CA names sent
SSL handshake has read 2048 bytes and written 489 bytes
---
```

External (bastion/public):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.acme.svc:443 -servername private.redwood.acme.svc -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Redwood, CN = Redwood Root CA
verify return:1
depth=1 C = US, O = Redwood, CN = Redwood Intermediate CA
verify return:1
depth=0 CN = private.redwood.acme.svc
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:CN = private.redwood.acme.svc
   i:CN = Redwood Intermediate CA
 1 s:CN = Redwood Intermediate CA
   i:CN = Redwood Root CA
 2 s:CN = Redwood Root CA
   i:CN = Redwood Root CA
---
```

Kevin (Support): That mismatch is suspicious. If the inline inspector terminates TLS and re-issues a cert, it often omits the intermediate in the server cert it presents to clients. Some clients will fetch AIA or expect the server to send the full chain. Since your app hosts are pinned to strict verify, they fail verification. Two immediate asks: 1) Can you capture a tcpdump of the ClientHello/ServerHello around the failing flow so we can see SNI and CERT lengths? 2) Can you paste the inspector config or vendor docs (some vendors have an option like "include full chain on re-sign" that may be off).

ACME Oncall: grabbed a short tcpdump excerpt from the failing host. We filtered by IP to the internal VIP and grepped TLS SNI. Looks like the inspector rewrites SNI to the upstream service name and re-signs with only the leaf cert: `TLS SNI "private.redwood.acme.svc" -> inspector.local` and then presents only leaf bytes.

We also found this in the inspector logs:
```
2026-03-16T02:12:07Z INFO tls-rewrite: re-signed cert; include_chain=false; original_sni=private.redwood.acme.svc; new_sni=inspector.local
```

Oliver K.: That explains the openssl behavior. Root cause here is the TLS-inspector re-signing without including the intermediate. A few remediation paths: 
- Enable "include_chain=true" (or equivalent) on the inspector so it serves leaf+intermediate to clients.
- If inspector cannot serve intermediate, add the intermediate cert to the system truststore on the internal hosts (quick workaround).
- Alternatively, configure the inspector to passthrough TLS for traffic to Redwood endpoints (preferred).

Kevin (Support): Also note: rotator uploaded a new bundle which included a cross-signed intermediate. If the inspector drops extras or reorders certs, some clients with stricter path-building may fail. We can reissue a rotation that embeds only the intermediate that's accepted by your inspector, but that's a customer-side bandaid — we recommend fixing the inspector.

ACME Oncall: Confirmed — enabling include_chain on the appliance fixed the curl verify error and 401s stopped. We still want to understand why some requests were 504s: those were timeouts while the app retried after TLS verify/hard-failed.

Kevin (Support): 504s were side-effect from retries; good to hear enabling include_chain fixed it. For completeness, here are reproducible steps we used to validate internally: 
```
# from a host behind inspector (failing path):
openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.acme.svc:443 -servername private.redwood.acme.svc -showcerts | sed -n '1,60p'
curl -v https://private.redwood.acme.svc/health -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" --resolve private.redwood.acme.svc:443:10.20.1.5
# from bastion (working path):
openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.acme.svc:443 -servername private.redwood.acme.svc -showcerts | sed -n '1,200p'
```

Oliver K.: We'll add a short KB note for support indicating: if customers use TLS-inspection that re-signs certs, ensure inspector preserves intermediate chain or allow passthrough to Redwood endpoints (and allow AIA/OCSP egress).

ACME Oncall: Thanks — that KB would be helpful. For our postmortem we'll note: rotation itself succeeded, but our inline TLS-inspector mutated the presented chain and caused strict-verifying hosts to fail.

Kevin (Support): Great summary. Marking thread resolved? :white_check_mark:
